colorRule: Each party gets a colour slot in alphabetical order of its electoral body acronym. The colour means nothing, and no party chose or paid for it. A party's acronym is always printed next to its colour, so nobody has to rely on colour alone.
orderRule: Cards are shuffled on every visit so no party is always first. Readers can switch to A–Z.
paletteSource: Kenneth L. Kelly, 'Twenty-two colors of maximum contrast' (1965), white/black removed, two high-contrast additions
